h: פָּרָשַׁת אַחֲרֵי מוֹת, ב׳ Acharei Mos, 2
Holy Longing Must Enter and Leave in Peace

p: In Rashi's commentary, from Toras Kohanim:
"What was told him in the first utterance?
It was compared to a sick man, etc.;
this one warned him more urgently than the first."
did not mention the punishment of death at all,
so he warned him more than the first;
after all, in the warning too
the punishment of death is written:
Also in the parable it is possible
that the sick man did not believe the first,
which is not so with the second,
And there is no difference at all
between the first warning and the second.
Also, Heaven forbid to say of Aharon
that he would act out of fear of punishment;
certainly he would fulfill the mitzvah of Hashem Yisbarach
that it says in the Midrash (Tanchuma, 6):
'In the light of the King's face is life,'" etc.;
that is, they entered the Pardes.
on the level of the Kohen Gadol
"On the first of Nissan they died, etc.;
it mentions their death on Yom Kippur,
that just as Yom Kippur atones,
And how would their death atone
that regarding the Holy of Holies it is written (Vayikra 16:17),
וְכָל אָדָם לֹא יִהְיֶה בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד
"And no man shall be in the Tent of Meeting,"
"and the likeness of their faces was the face of a man";
and so the Kohen Gadol saw
and nourished his eyes from the Shechinah.
אִיתָא (בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ חֵלֶק ב קכא, א)
it says (in the holy Zohar II 121a),
"'And wisdom, from where is it found?'
From the place called the Holy of Holies."
and they were like Ben Azzai,
give up his life to see,
just as they gave up their lives;
so what would the warning help,
that he not enter with self-sacrifice,
for then he is like Rabbi Akiva,
who is worthy to make use of My glory,
as they said of Rabbi Akiva
מָשְׁכֵנִי אַחֲרֶיךָ נָּרוּצָה (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים א, ד)
'Draw me, we will run after You'" (Shir HaShirim 1:4).
